sentences.text: 5. The appellant/ Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited being aggrieved by the judgement and award passed by the learned Trial Court has come up with the instant appeal.

Although different grounds were taken by the appellant at the time of preferring this appeal but at the time of argument learned advocate for the appellant confined only to the grounds that the learned Trial Judge erred in holding that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving without the valid driving licience and by not granting liberty to the appellant/ Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited to recover from the owner of the offending vehicle.
6.

sentences.text: Learned advocate submits that the claimants respondent Nos. 1 and 2 has filed all relevant documents but has not filed the driving licence of the driver.
Thus, it is to be presumed that the driver did not have any valid driving licence.

Although the owner of the vehicle being respondent No. 3 did not appear to contest this appeal but learned advocate for the claimants respondent Nos. 1 and 2 appears and dispute the submission of the learned advocate for the appellant and submits that the relevant documents were placed before the learned Trial Court.

7. Upon perusal of the judgment and award passed by the learned Trial Court it appears that the learned Trial Judge while considering the claim case was pleased to make the following observations:

3 "22.

entities.text: Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance Co. ... vs Saraswati Kar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has not come up with any sort of evidence to set up a story that the deceased was negligent in the accident.
Further it is revealed from the Exhibit-3 series that deceased had a valid driving licence.
There is, therefore, no iota of evidence to indicate that the deceased was negligent in the accident.
So, it is proved that the deceased had no negligence in the accident.
I find further that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

Viewed thus, the driver of the offending vehicle was solely responsible for the accident and this fact is accordingly,
established in the case".
8. Although the driving licence was not filed by the claimants respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 but from the seizure list it appears that the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid driving licence.

Thus,
this Court does not find any error in the observation made by the learned Trial Judge in paragraph 22 of the judgment and award.

Moreover, the appellant/ Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited did not take any steps to examine either the owner of the offending vehicle or the driver of the offending vehicle or the investigating officer who has conducted the investigation.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: Hence the plea of the appellant that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence cannot be sustained.
9. In the facts and circumstances this Court does not find any error in the judgment and award passed by the learned Trial Court.
10. Thus, this appeal stands dismissed.
11. The judgment and award dated 30.08.2024 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Fast Tract 3rd Court, Sadar, Paschim Medinipur in MAC Case No. 549 of 2020 is affirmed.
